title: Grade 5 French — Wed, May 27
description: Family & Home (La Famille et la Maison) — Day 3 of 5
subject: french

questions.question: What is the French word for 'mother'?
questions.explanation: 'Mère' = mother. Père = father, Frère = brother, Sœur = sister.

questions.question: How do you say 'grandmother' in French?
questions.explanation: 'Grand-mère' = grandmother. Grand-père = grandfather, Oncle = uncle, Tante = aunt.

questions.question: What does 'J'ai un frère et une sœur' mean?
options: I have a mother and a father
I have a brother and a sister
I have an uncle and an aunt
I have a son and a daughter
questions.explanation: 'J'ai un frère et une sœur' = 'I have a brother and a sister'. Frère = brother, sœur = sister.

questions.question: What is the French word for 'house'?
questions.explanation: 'Maison' = house. Appartement = apartment, École = school, Magasin = shop/store.

questions.question: How do you say 'bedroom' in French?
questions.explanation: 'Chambre' (or 'chambre à coucher') = bedroom. Cuisine = kitchen, Salon = living room, Salle de bains = bathroom.

questions.question: What does 'la cuisine' refer to?
questions.explanation: 'La cuisine' = the kitchen. It also means 'cooking/cuisine' — the room where cooking happens.

questions.question: How do you say 'I live in a house' in French?
questions.explanation: 'J'habite dans une maison' = 'I live in a house'. 'Habiter' means 'to live/reside'.

questions.question: What is the French word for 'cousin' (male)?
questions.explanation: 'Cousin' = male cousin. 'Cousine' = female cousin. Neveu = nephew, Oncle = uncle.

questions.question: 'Le salon' in a house refers to:
questions.explanation: 'Le salon' = the living room. It's where the family typically spends time together.

questions.question: How do you say 'My family is big' in French?
questions.explanation: 'Ma famille est grande' = 'My family is big'. 'Famille' is feminine, so 'grande' (not grand).

questions.question: What does 'les parents' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Les parents' = the parents (in common use). Note: it can also mean 'relatives' in a broader sense.

questions.question: What is the French word for 'garden'?
questions.explanation: 'Jardin' = garden. Garage = garage, Grenier = attic, Couloir = corridor/hallway.

questions.question: How do you say 'I have two sisters' in French?
'La salle de bains' is:
questions.explanation: 'La salle de bains' = the bathroom (literally 'the bath room'). In French homes, the toilet may be separate.

questions.question: What does 'Où habites-tu?' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Où habites-tu?' = 'Where do you live?' (informal). 'Où' = where, 'habiter' = to live.
